result.summary: github.com/tidwall/pretty is a pure JSON formatting library: pretty-printing, compacting, colorizing and stripping comments. It imports only bytes, encoding/json, sort and strconv. I checked the single file, including its init function, and found no file, process, network or environment access, and no encoded payloads.

findings.title: init assigns default terminal color style
findings.detail: init() only builds the TerminalStyle struct of ANSI color codes and a byte-escaping Append function. It has no side effects beyond setting a package variable.

capabilities.explanation: Comes from harmless calls: json.Unmarshal in parsestr (reflection-based decoding), sort.Stable on byKeyVal through the sort.Interface, and the Style.Append callback that Color calls. None of these runs code taken from data. They are ordinary JSON decoding, sorting and a caller-supplied formatting hook.

No network code exists in the package. Its only imports are bytes, encoding/json, sort and strconv. The capability is an artifact of the conservative call graph: json.Unmarshal's reflective dispatch to Unmarshaler/TextUnmarshaler implementations can reach types such as those in package net. Here it only ever decodes into a plain string.
